newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Fujimori to restart activities Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori to restart activities Wednesday.

text.p: Peru's President Alberto Fujimori, recovering from mouth surgery he underwent at Lima's top cancer hospital, will gradually restart official activities on Wednesday, Government Palace officials said.
Fujimori was scheduled to have a second post-operative checkup on Tuesday and spend the rest of the day resting in isolation, the officials added.

"The head of state will not receive visits nor answer telephone calls for medical reasons. From Wednesday May 14 he will return, progressively, to his usual activities," the president's office said in a statement.
Fujimori, 58, spent nine hours on Sunday in Lima's National Institute of Neoplastic Illnesses, which specializes in operations to treat or prevent cancer.
He is due to leave on Thursday for the United States on a personal visit when he will attend his eldest daughter Keiko's graduation ceremony in Boston.

Keiko, who has acted as Peru's first lady since Fujimori's split from his wife in 1995, said her father was not suffering from a serious illness and should be fully recovered from the operation within a week.
She denied he was travelling to the United States for further medical treatment.
